project_type: Hybrid: Python backend (kiro_crew, an AI agent) + TypeScript/React frontend dashboard (website/). This task touches the output-redaction seam that exists in both.
build_system: Backend: setuptools via pyproject.toml, editable install with uv. Frontend: Vite (tsc -b && vite build). Node 22 via nvm; npm available.
test_framework: Backend: pytest 9.0.3 (from [dependency-groups].dev in pyproject.toml). Frontend: vitest (npm run test:website runs `vitest run --coverage`).
build_command: Backend: `uv pip install -e '.[dev]'` (or the dependency-group). Frontend: `cd website && npm ci && npm run build`.
test_command: Backend targeted: `python3 -m pytest test/test_diagnostics.py test/test_redaction_mirror_parity.py test/test_security.py -q`. Frontend targeted: `cd website && npx vitest run src/test/ src/utils/` (or `npm run test:website`).
verification_instructions: 1) Backend: run pytest over test_security.py, test_diagnostics.py, test_redaction_mirror_parity.py and confirm green. 2) Frontend: run vitest over the sanitize tests and confirm green, and run `cd website && npm run build` to confirm the eager entry chunk still compiles (guards the Safari-14 no-lookbehind constraint at build time). 3) Confirm test_redaction_mirror_parity.py still passes (JWT credential-pattern parity untouched).
snapshot_or_generated_files: i18n locale files under website/src/i18n/locales/*.json contain the `utils.sanitize.redacted_suspicious_url` key. en.manual.json is the source-of-truth English string. If a NEW i18n key is introduced it must be added to en.manual.json at minimum; other locales fall back. No codegen/snapshot regeneration command is strictly required for redaction logic, but check whether the repo has an i18n key-sync check in CI.
setup_instructions: Backend: from repo root `/projects/sandbox/KiroCrew`, install dev deps into the active env (pytest is NOT preinstalled): `uv pip install -e '.[dev]'` or `uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio hypothesis`. Frontend: `cd website && npm ci`. Network is OPEN_INTERNET so installs are allowed.
environment_constraints: Network mode OPEN_INTERNET (installs allowed). No Docker required. CRITICAL platform constraint: the frontend sanitize.ts is in the eagerly-loaded entry chunk; vite.config.ts declares no build.target so the default 'modules'/safari14 floor applies. Module-level regex literals MUST NOT use lookbehind ((?<=...)/(?<!...)) — esbuild rewrites them to `new RegExp()` which throws at module-eval time and blanks the dashboard. test_redaction_mirror_parity.py::test_frontend_omits_every_lookbehind_on_purpose enforces this across the whole file.
contribution_requirements: Backend/frontend redaction PARITY is enforced by test/test_redaction_mirror_parity.py, but ONLY for the two JWT credential alternatives in _CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS (byte-identical in the frontend body, minus the leading lookbehind). The EXFIL_PATTERNS / EXFIL_QUERY_MIN_LEN / exempt-host logic are NOT pinned by that test, so the frontend exfiltration exemption may diverge in mechanism from the backend as long as (a) the JWT parity test stays green and (b) no lookbehind is introduced. Any security-policy change must be reflected in docs/system-specs/modules/security.md and the pinning tests.
key_patterns: Backend `_exfil_url_warning` (security.py ~line 10440) is the single shared per-URL classifier for scan_exfiltration_urls + redact_exfiltration_urls. Its layered order is: (1) S3-presigned exemption, (2) _HARD_CREDENTIAL_RE across full path+query [UNCONDITIONAL], (3) _contains_fixed_credential across full payload [UNCONDITIONAL], (4) multi-pass percent-decode + fail-closed saturation [UNCONDITIONAL], (5) _EXFIL_PERCENT_RE heavy-percent-encoding [UNCONDITIONAL — 20+ CONSECUTIVE octets], (6) THEN selects heuristic_query for the base64-blob/length heuristics, applying carve-outs: OAuth-endpoint param stripping (banner path only), self Slack app-create alias, and `_dom in exempt_hosts` -> heuristic_query=''. The exempt_hosts set comes from a companion CredentialPolicy (_exfil_exempt_hosts), NOT config.json, and skips ONLY base64-blob + length heuristics. The frontend sanitizeExfiltrationUrls does NONE of this layering — it is a flat `query.length>=200 || EXFIL_PATTERNS.test(query)` check with no unconditional-vs-heuristic split and no host exemption. Confirmed false-positive hosts from the issue: `github.com` (issues/new?title=...&body=...) and `monitorportal.amazon.com`.

website/src/test/sanitizeCredentials.test.ts (frontend test pattern to follow for new sanitizeExfiltrationUrls tests)
